roleHint.auditIds: Audit counts, dead stock, cash review.
roleHint.approverIds: Damaged, expired, lost, found and counted stock. Nobody listed = anyone who may approve inventory.

set.anyOne: Any one of them is enough
set.anyOneHint: No: every approver listed must say yes.

seatHint.owner: Handles their own top clients; approves the plan.
seatHint.crrSc: Calls existing clients on SCOT; win-back calls.
seatHint.osr: Takes orders from existing clients at the office.
seatHint.crm: Runs the steps after an order and collections.
seatHint.nbdSc: Owns new enquiries and the funnel.
seatHint.salesRep: Meets new clients in the field.
seatHint.marketing: Brings enquiries (can be an outside agency).
seatHint.ea: Helps the owner keep the plan moving.
seatHint.pc: Follows up that steps happen on time.

tagRule.top20: the top 20% of customers by gross profit in 12 months: they go to the owner.
tagRule.bottom20: the bottom 20% by gross profit: review or stop.
tagRule.new: fewer than {{orders}} orders or first order in the last {{newDays}} days (Customer rules).
tagRule.lost: no order for {{lost}} days, or marked lost on a call.
tagRule.vampire: in the top 40% by sales, but pays later than their credit days and earns gross profit below the middle.
tagRule.owners: the owner's own customers (or handled by the owner).

s.unlockBody: Anyone with edit access can change it again. It will need approval once more.
s.locked: The plan is sent for approval or approved: unlock it to change it.
s.monthsEditedBody: Some months were changed by hand. Saving this works every month out again from the year and the quarters.
s.yearHint: Last year's actual turnover (before GST) and gross profit, then how much to grow.
s.quartersHint: Each quarter's growth over the one before. Seasons and holidays are already counted. Fine-tune a quarter with − and +; the year total stays.
s.monthsHint: Months follow working days, seasons and growth within each quarter (each quarter's total stays). Change a month by hand with the pencil.
s.monthGrowth: Growth from month to month inside a quarter
s.restOfPlan: You changed this month. What should happen to the rest of the plan?
s.keepYear: Keep the year total — adjust other months
s.keepYearHint: The other months change so the year stays {{total}}.
s.weeksHint: Weeks run Monday to Sunday. Part weeks at a month's edge can join the next full week. Each week's target follows its working days; set day by day if days differ.
s.joinWeeks: Join part weeks at month edges
s.weeksCheck: {{month}}'s weeks add up to {{weeks}} = its month target {{target}}. All 12 months add up to {{year}}.

btHint.manufacturing: Fix the production plan (PMS) first: sales can't sell what isn't made.
btHint.trading: Stock and margins by item matter most.
btHint.services: Capacity (people's time) is what you sell.
btHint.retail: Many small customers; footfall and repeat buying.
btHint.projects: Few large orders, long cycles, milestone payments.

stHint.export: Adds a sampling flow and English CRM.
stHint.government: Adds a liaison person and a tender flow.

s.seatsHint: One person may hold several seats.
s.seatsSummary: {{used}} of {{of}} seats in use · {{people}} people · {{empty}} empty
s.splitHint: How the year target splits between existing clients (CRR) and new ones (NBD), and each person's month-by-month target.
s.ownerAmount: Sales from the owner's own clients this year
s.ownerAmountHint: Taken out of CRR; the rest is shared by the CRR seats.
s.scienceOk: Targets add up and no rule is broken.

warn.ownerOverCrr: The owner's amount is more than the whole CRR target.
warn.noLeadSources: NBD has a target but no lead sources.

s.customerRulesHint: These rules drive the automatic tags and the win-back calls.
s.newUntilOrders: A new customer stays new until
s.winBackHint: Sleeping and lost customers go to the CRR SC's win-back calls.
s.vampireHint: Big buyers who pay late and earn little.
s.afterOrderHint: The steps every order goes through. They run as a real FMS flow: each step's doer is whoever sits in its seat.
s.openFlow: Open the flow in the FMS builder
s.nbdHint: Where leads come from, what the enquiry form asks, when an enquiry becomes a lead, and the funnel's stages.
s.formFieldsHint: Name, mobile, city, source and requirement are always asked.
s.questionsHint: An enquiry becomes a lead when all are answered Yes.
s.stagesHint: Planned days in each stage: longer than that is stuck.
s.wonLost: Won and Lost come after the last stage.
s.calendarHint: Holidays and weekly offs are shared with HR and the working-time calculator: change them here or in HR.
s.seasonsHint: Peak, good and slow months lift or lower their share of the year.
s.tapMonth: Tap a month to change its season.
s.roundingHint: Targets in round figures. Every level still adds up exactly: what can't be rounded goes to the biggest part.
s.roundingExample: e.g. the first month {{month}}, its first week {{week}}.

masters.importHint: Put the field names in the first row: {{fields}}. Dates as DD/MM/YYYY. All rows are added, or none if something needs fixing.
masters.paste: Or paste rows here (from Excel or Google Sheets)
masters.removeBody: It leaves the list. Records that already use it keep their text, and its key can be used again.
masters.rowsSubtitle: Enter it once. Every module reads the same rows.
masters.sheetHint: Share the sheet as "Anyone with the link can view" first.

lib.subtitle: Ready-made masters by industry. Pick one and it is yours, fields and all.
lib.tagline: Enter it once. Every module reads the same customer, item and person.

keys.emptyBody: Make a key for each outside tool (Tally connector, a website form, a sheet script) so you can stop one without touching the others.
keys.name: What is this key for?
keys.nameHint: For example "Tally connector" or "Website enquiry form".
keys.onceHint: Copy it now and keep it somewhere safe. It is shown only this once; after this you see only its last 4 characters.
keys.revokeBody: Anything using this key stops working at once. This can't be undone; make a new key instead.
keys.serverHint: Outside tools call this address with a key. The key works with the rights of the person who made it.
keys.title: API keys

hooks.emptyBody: A webhook tells another system the moment something happens, for example a new order or a stock move.
hooks.subtitle: Chosen events are posted to your address, signed with a secret, and retried if your side is down.
hooks.title: Webhooks
hooks.urlHint: An https:// address on the internet. Addresses inside your own network are refused.

drive.counts: {{on}} files in Drive · {{waiting}} waiting to move
drive.ownerOnly: Only the account owner can connect Google Drive.
drive.paused: New files stay on the server again. Files already in Drive still open.
drive.secretHint: Kept encrypted on the server and never shown again.
drive.tickFirst: Tick steps 1 to 3 when they are done.
drive.nowServer: Right now, files are kept on the {{app}} server and are part of the nightly backup.

back.error: Google Drive could not be connected. See the message on this page.
back.expired: That sign-in took too long or was already used. Press Connect Drive again.
back.owner: Only the account owner can connect Google Drive.
back.denied: Google was not allowed access. Press Connect Drive and choose Allow.
back.signin: Sign in to MONO first, then press Connect Drive again.

project.title: Make a Google Cloud project and turn on the Google Drive API
project.body: Sign in with the company's Google account. Create a project (any name, e.g. MONO), then press Enable on "Google Drive API".

consent.title: Set up the OAuth consent screen and publish it
consent.body: Audience: External. Add the scope below (only files this app makes). Then press "Publish app": while it is in Testing, Google disconnects after 7 days.

client.title: Create an OAuth client (Web application)
client.body: Clients → Create client → Web application. Under "Authorised redirect URIs" paste this address exactly, then Create.

connect.title: Paste the Client ID and secret, then connect

see.q: What can {{app}} see in my Drive?
see.a: Only the files {{app}} puts there itself (Google's "drive.file" permission). It cannot open or list anything else.

existing.q: What happens to files uploaded before?
existing.a: They stay on the {{app}} server and in its backups. Only new files move to Drive, about a minute after upload.

pause.a: Yes. Stop sending files keeps new uploads on the server again. Files already in Drive still open from {{app}}.

publish.q: Why must the app be published?
publish.a: Google ends sign-ins of apps in Testing after 7 days. Publishing your own internal app needs no review for this permission.

cost.a: No. It uses your Drive storage (15 GB free per Google account, more with Google Workspace).

backup.q: Are Drive files in the nightly backup?
backup.a: No, Google keeps them. The backup keeps the database (which knows every file) and files still on the server.

pwa.hint: Opens like an app, faster, with notifications.
pwa.iosHint: Tap Share, then "Add to Home Screen".

errors.crashedBody: It has been reported. Reload to try again; your saved work is safe.
errors.noneBody: Nothing has gone wrong. Errors from the server, the worker and people's browsers show up here.
errors.subtitle: Errors are grouped by kind and counted. A fixed one comes back if it happens again.

support.subtitle: Whom to ask, a help ticket, and the guides for every module.
support.ticketBody: Raise a help ticket: the right person fixes it, and you see where it stands.
